messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Spanish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Spanish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Cuando lo vi en el gran desierto, Le grité que tuviera piedad de mí, Sea lo que seas ya sea sombra o hombre seguro.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Spanish Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |------------|-----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | Quando | temporal conjunction “when” | Cuando | “When” | OK | | vidi | verb “saw” (past) | vi | “saw” | OK | | costui | demonstrative pronoun “him” | lo | “him” | OK | | nel | preposition “in” | en | “in” | OK | | gran | adjective “great” | gran | “great” | OK | | diserto | noun “desert” | desierto | “desert” | OK | | Miserere | imperative “have pity” | tuviera piedad | “have pity” (subjunctive) | OK | | di | preposition “of / on” | de | “of” | OK | | me | pronoun “me” | mí | “me” | OK | | gridi | verb “cried / shouted” | grité | “I shouted” | OK | | a | preposition “to” | Le | “to him” (indirect object pronoun) | **UNNECESSARY** (Spanish uses the clitic *le* instead of a preposition) | | lui | pronoun “him” (dative) | Le | “him” | OK | | qual | relative pronoun “whatever” | lo | “whatever” (part of *lo que*) | OK | | che | relative connector “that” | que | “that” | OK | | tu | pronoun “you” (2nd sg) | seas | “you are” (subjunctive) | OK | | sii | verb “be” (subjunctive) | seas | “are” (subjunctive) | OK | | od (1st) | conjunction “or” | ya sea | “or” (resultative) | OK | | ombra | noun “shade” | sombra | “shade” | OK | | od (2nd) | conjunction “or” | o | “or” | OK | | omo | noun “man” | hombre | “man” | OK | | certo | adjective “certain / real” | seguro | “certain / real” | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY:** *a* – the preposition is omitted in Spanish because the indirect object pronoun *le* already conveys the “to” meaning. No other source tokens are missing or incorrectly rendered.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Spanish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 64** - Original: `Cuando lo vi en el gran desierto,` - Issue: none - Corrected: `Cuando lo vi en el gran desierto,`
- **Line 65** - Original: `Le grité que tuviera piedad de mí,` - Issue: **GRAMMAR** – the subordinate clause should use the present subjunctive to match the imperative request. - Corrected: `Le grité que tenga piedad de mí,`
- **Line 66** - Original: `Sea lo que seas ya sea sombra o hombre seguro.` - Issue: none - Corrected: `Sea lo que seas ya sea sombra o hombre seguro.`
```text Cuando lo vi en el gran desierto, Le grité que tenga piedad de mí, Sea lo que seas ya sea sombra o hombre seguro. ```
